Notes: THE MOST IMPORTANT ROW IN THE FILE. Every box the game draws goes through this one - card faces, tiles, the strip above the cards, the keeper's number, the celebration window, all of it. It is drawn from beerhall_panel, which is LIGHT OAK so the tint lands on it: each screen still passes its own colour and the wood arrives wearing it. Blank the Image cell and every box goes back to a flat colour.

Dialogs and the celebration window. Tint is `no` - this one is drawn finished, dark stained oak with a brass frame and four corner studs, and tinting it would only muddy it. The studs live inside the 28px corner, so they never stretch however big the window gets.
A brass-edged plaque. Untinted, because a button should look the same on every screen.
Lit from above - the same plaque under the lamp.
Pushed in. Same wood, bevel flipped.
Greyed out. No image on purpose: a disabled button should not look like a thing you can press.
THE 'YOU ARE HERE' BOX for a controller or the arrow keys. Drawn OVER whatever the button already looks like, so leave Fill empty or you will paint out the button underneath.
The one button on a screen you are most likely to want: PLAY, START, CONTINUE. It wears the lit plaque all the time.
A beer mat: cream card with the blue-and-white Bavarian lozenge along the top and bottom. Text Colour is DARK here because the card is light - the one place in the game where that is true.
An unselected tab.
The empty glass. Loading bars, keeper stamina, a talent's progress.
The beer, with a head on it.
A line between things. Fill is the line's colour; Border Width is ignored.

A FONT ROW. No box - only Font, Size and Text Colour are read. Bonum is a Bookman: heavy, wide and warm, which is the shape of a beer label. THIS ONE CELL IS THE BIGGEST SINGLE CHANGE IN THE ROUND - the default Godot font is the most recognisable thing on a screen. Swap it for a Fraktur if you find one you like; blackletter belongs on the big titles only, never on the body.
Schola is a Century Schoolbook: warm, sturdy and made to be read. Keep the body a serif you can read at 12 points - a Fraktur here would be unreadable and would look like a costume.
Captions and the quiet notes under things.

BEER GOLD, and the only bright thing on screen. In Marcinelle the eye is led by ONE hot colour against a warm neutral ground - Asterix does it with the red of the pants, Franquin with the yellow of the Marsupilami. Everything you want pressed is this and nothing else is.
Stained oak, almost black. The inside of a beer hall at night, and dark enough that a 1px black outline still reads against it.
column17: almost black. The inside of a beer hall at night.

Notes: Walnut. One step up from the ground so a panel reads as sitting ON something.
Cream enamel. NOT white: pure white on this ground is a hole, and the comics this is drawn from print on paper, never on light.
BURNT ORANGE - late autumn, and the warm half of the pair. Attacking, and the ATK tag on a Star's ability.
BAVARIAN SKY BLUE - the cool half. The blue-and-white lozenge is the one piece of real Bavaria in the palette and it earns its place.
The four tiers in ladder order. Autumn: slate, moss, copper, plum. They are deliberately MUTED - a tier colour is a label, not a feature, and four more bright colours would fight the accent.
